belief: Grieving shows a lack of faith.
origins: Some Christians are told to “be strong,” “rejoice, they are in a better place,” or “don’t cry.” Those words may come from love, but they can leave mourners feeling that tears are a spiritual failure. We then grieve privately or pretend to be fine.
teaches: “Jesus wept.” He wept at Lazarus’s tomb, knowing He was about to raise him. Isaiah describes the Messiah as “a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief.” Jesus said, “Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.” Solomon wrote, “A time to weep and a time to laugh.” Paul says we do not “grieve like the rest, who are without hope,” which does not mean that we do not grieve. The psalmist says that God keeps our tears. Tears and trust are not opposites. Deep grief often reflects deep love.
self_statements: Strong believers do not cry this much.
If I really trusted God, I would be at peace.
I should be rejoicing, not mourning.
People will think my faith is weak.
errors: Insisting that I should not grieve.
Believing faith and sorrow cannot coexist.
Feeling sad and concluding that my faith is lacking.
questions: Did Jesus grieve? What does that tell me?
Who told me that grief is a lack of faith?
Can I trust God and cry at the same time?
What do my tears say about my love?
Who can I grieve with honestly?
truth: Grief does not show a lack of faith. Jesus wept, and He blesses those who mourn. I can grieve with hope, cry honestly, and trust God at the same time.
hw_truths: Faith and sorrow can live together.
log: Each week, note one time you cried and one time you trusted God in the sorrow.
actions: Notice that Jesus wept before He acted.
Share your grief with someone who does not rush you.
Pray Psalm 56:8 and others that voice sorrow.
prayer: Jesus, You wept. Thank You that tears are not failure. Meet me in my sorrow, give me honest friends, and hold me in hope. Amen.
hw_questions: Who told me grief is weak faith?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Jesus wept, so my tears do not mean a lack of faith.”
